subject: Unexplained usage multiplier on Nov invoice
messages:
From: David Lane <david.lane@greengriddb.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, accounts@greengriddb.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Unexplained usage multiplier on Nov invoice

Hi Irene,

Hope you’re well. We just received our November invoice and noticed our token usage (line items) appears to be ~4x higher than expected for Nov 14–15. We’re attaching the PDF extract from our billing dashboard — the numbers don’t line up with our internal telemetry.

Quick summary:
- Expected token count for Nov 14: ~1.2M
- Invoice shows: ~4.8M (same period)
- No major traffic spike on our side — we checked request rates and didn’t see the multiplier.

Could you confirm whether there was a service incident on your side that might have caused duplicate counting/retries? This is material for our month-end budget — we’ll need a prompt explanation and any proposed remediation or credits.

Attachment: usage_nov14_invoice.pdf (PDF)

Thanks,
David Lane
Head of Platform, GreenGrid Inc
David.Lane@greengriddb.com
(415) 555-0198
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexplained usage multiplier on Nov invoice

Hi David — thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the invoice extract. I’ve looped in engineering (Rishi) and billing ops (Neha) to investigate immediately.

Immediate next steps from our side:
1) Engineering will scan the serving logs and token accounting for Nov 14–15 and look for retry/duplication patterns.
2) Billing ops will reproduce the invoice slice and flag rows that look anomalous.
3) I’ll propose a provisional credit while we validate root cause so your cashflow isn’t impacted.

Can you confirm whether we should apply any provisional credit to next month’s invoice or process an immediate refund if confirmed? Also attaching your original invoice again for our records.

Attachment: usage_nov14_invoice.pdf (forwarded)

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T11:27:00-08:00
Subject: Fw: Unexplained usage multiplier on Nov invoice — preliminary findings

Forwarding preliminary notes from ops scan:

On 2026-11-14 03:42–04:15 UTC we saw a short control-plane incident that caused several in-flight requests to be retried at the routing layer. The retry loop doubled requests for a subset of model shards, and due to a token-accounting edge case the retry path incremented token counters again instead of piggybacking on the original request’s usage.

Log excerpt (anonymized):

[2026-11-14T03:43:02Z] INFO request_id=abc123 route=us-west2 model=redwood-v2 seq=-- RETRY dispatch duplicated call (retry_count=1)
[2026-11-14T03:43:02Z] INFO token_accounting request_id=abc123 tokens=3122 incremented_by=3122
[2026-11-14T03:43:02Z] INFO token_accounting request_id=abc123 tokens=3122 incremented_by=3122 (retry path)

Initial estimate: for requests in the impacted window we’re seeing an average duplication factor between 3.8x–4.2x depending on shard group. We’re running a dedup script now to compute affected tokens per account and will produce a CSV with exact numbers.

Attachment: investigation_log_snippet.txt (txt)

Action items:
- Run dedup accounting job for GreenGrid (ETA 24 hours).
- Prepare provisional credit proposal (Irene + Neha).
- Postmortem to cover root cause and plan to prevent double-counting (engineering change + accounting test).

-Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: David Lane <david.lane@greengriddb.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, accounts@greengriddb.com
Date: 2026-11-16T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexplained usage multiplier on Nov invoice — provisional credit and next steps

Hi David — quick update following Rishi’s analysis.

Summary of findings (preliminary):
- There was an internal retry incident on 2026-11-14 that caused duplicate token increments for a subset of calls.
- Preliminary dedup job indicates GreenGrid saw ~3.95x token inflation for the impacted window.
- We are confident the extra charges are due to our accounting bug and will be removed/credited.

Provisional remediation we can offer immediately:
- Provisional credit of $7,200 applied to your Nov invoice balance (we calculated this using the dedup estimate; exact number subject to final dedup job).
- We can apply the credit to your Dec invoice or issue a refund — please confirm preference.
- We’ll run the final accounting job within 24 hours and produce a reconciliation CSV and a short credit agreement for signature (DocuSign link below).

DocuSign (pre-approved adjustment): docusign://adjustment-GG-1234
Reconciliation link (internal): https://redwood.console/charges/GG-1234

Next steps on engineering: a permanent fix to prevent retry path from double-incrementing tokens is in flight; estimated release early next week. Postmortem with timeline + test coverage will be shared within 3 business days.

Attachment: provisional_credit_agreement.pdf (PDF)

Please let me know whether you want the credit applied to Dec or refunded. Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll make this right and follow up with the full postmortem.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
From: David Lane <david.lane@greengriddb.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: accounts@greengriddb.com
Date: 2026-11-18T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexplained usage multiplier on Nov invoice — provisional credit and next steps

Irene — thanks for the quick investigation and the provisional credit offer. We’re happy to apply the $7,200 credit to December’s invoice rather than a refund.

Two quick asks:
1) Can you confirm the exact date the permanent fix will be in production? We’d like a heads-up before next month’s billing closes.
2) Please include a CSV reconciliation that shows raw tokens, deduped tokens, and the credit calculation for our finance team.

Once we have the reconciliation we’ll sign the adjustment doc. Appreciate the speed here.

Best,
David
